requirements.requirement: opsadmin user account created on node1
requirements.summary: useradd created opsadmin (cmd-637be6d816974631); getent passwd confirms presence pre- and post-restart (cmd-ef436aa231a44285, cmd-09a72e3ef7c04548).

requirements.requirement: Specified ed25519 public key installed for opsadmin SSH access
requirements.summary: authorized_keys populated with the exact requested key string, 700/600 perms and correct ownership set; content verified unchanged after restart including a live SSH handshake.

requirements.requirement: SSH configured to require key-based authentication (no password/keyboard-interactive)
requirements.summary: 99-key-only.conf drop-in sets PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no / AuthenticationMethods publickey; sshd -T for opsadmin confirms these values both before and after restart, and opsadmin's password is locked.

requirements.requirement: sshd able to actually run and serve connections (implicit prerequisite for 'SSH access')
requirements.summary: Baseline node had no host keys and no /run/sshd, so sshd could not start at all; executor generated host keys, created /run/sshd, and added a tmpfiles.d rule to persist it. Post-restart evidence shows ssh.socket active, /run/sshd recreated by the rule, and a live TCP handshake returning the SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p banner.

requirements.requirement: Configuration survives a restart (implicit for a persistent SSH access/policy requirement)
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline captured (boot_id 92ec88af, ssh active, opsadmin+policy verified) via cmd-e06f825ab84e4659/cmd-559d01b45d8c4a0f; reboot acknowledged and observed as a real outage (cmd-bf1755f1a647478c, connection resets in cmd-357efc0b236947af/cmd-2563d668b6974d7c); new boot_id confirmed (cmd-b128abf0a6634ffa, matches global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity); post-restart state shows ssh.socket active, /run/sshd recreated by tmpfiles, opsadmin/key/password-lock intact, key-only policy still enforced, and a live handshake (cmd-09a72e3ef7c04548).

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: opsadmin was created on node1, the exact specified ed25519 key was installed with correct permissions, and SSH was configured and verified (via sshd -T and a live handshake) to require key-based authentication only, with password login locked. The node had a broken sshd baseline (no host keys, no /run/sshd, no tmpfiles rule for it) which the executor correctly diagnosed and fixed as a necessary prerequisite. A full, well-instrumented restart cycle (healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart recovery of SSH, account, and policy) directly demonstrates the configuration persists across a reboot. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: No independent evidence outside the executor's own commands (e.g., an actual external SSH client login attempt with the private key) was captured; sshd -T policy output and a raw TCP banner grab are strong but not a full end-to-end auth test.
Only a single restart cycle was observed; no evidence of behavior across multiple reboots or other failure modes (e.g., power loss) beyond the one native systemctl reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: user/key/config creation for the task (cmd-637be6d816974631, cmd-c4bfe3b78c2145ba), necessary prerequisite fixes for a base image that shipped without SSH host keys or a /run/sshd tmpfiles rule (cmd-c42339248a4f49d0, cmd-c4bfe3b78c2145ba, cmd-0c92b3c9cfa44e62), a no-op re-enable of an already-enabled ssh.socket (cmd-ef436aa231a44285), and the restart-evidence protocol (cmd-bf1755f1a647478c, cmd-357efc0b236947af, cmd-2563d668b6974d7c, cmd-b128abf0a6634ffa). No abandoned files, failed services, or weakened security controls are present in the after_executor snapshot (failed-services empty, package-health clean). The lifecycle diff shows only expected changes (new boot id, sshd now listening on 22 with an active service, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs regenerated post-reboot).
